newsitem.title: USA: Glickman sets busy bilateral agenda for IGC meet.
newsitem.headline: Glickman sets busy bilateral agenda for IGC meet.

text.p: U.S. Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman said Wednesday he will met with the Argentine and British agriculture ministers while in London this week for the International Grain Council's annual meeting.

Glickman also said he would meet with Canadian Natural Resources Minister Ralph Goodale, who still oversees the Canadian Wheat Board after recently switching from his former post as agriculture minister.
A fourth meeting is scheduled with a representative from the Australian Wheat Board, Glickman said.
Glickman spoke to reporters after a Senate Agriculture Committee hearing on prospects for US agricultural trade.

Glickman said he would use his speech on Thursday to the IGC to expound on that theme, including the serious concerns the U.S. has about an EU labeling proposal that would require the segregation of genetically-modified corn, soybeans and other crops throughout the marketing chain.
U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky told the farm panel that the EU could potentially disrupt $4.0 to $5.0 billion in U.S. agricultural exports to the region.
During the hearing, Glickman also repeated that the U.S. would not tolerate a "market-disrupting" surge of wheat and barley imports from Canada.

A few years ago, the U.S. imposed a one-year quota on wheat shipments from Canada and the issue remains a touchy one between the two countries. The U.S. and Canada will hold bilateral grain talks on June 27.
Meanwhile, Argentina has been waiting for USDA to finalize new meat trade regulations that would clear the way for that country to export 20,000 tonnes of beef to the U.S.
Glickman acknowledged he would probably discuss the issue with the Argentine minister, but could not say yet when Argentina would be granted access to the U.S. meat market.
Glickman also plans to visit a farm outside Kent while in England, aides said.
